questions.question: How can a driver check if a road is becoming icy?

options.text: Open the window and feel the side mirror for ice.

questions.correctAnswerText: Open the window and feel the side mirror for ice.
questions.explanation: To check if the road is becoming icy, open your window and touch the side mirror, mirror support, or antenna. If ice has formed on these items, the road is likely becoming icy.

questions.question: What should you do if someone is tailgating you?

options.text: Leave more space between your vehicle and the one ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Leave more space between your vehicle and the one ahead.
questions.explanation: If someone is tailgating you, increase the distance between your car and the car ahead. This gives you more room to stop smoothly and makes it easier for the tailgater to pass you.

questions.question: Most heavy trucks with manual transmissions need ____ to shift gears.
questions.explanation: Most heavy trucks with manual transmissions require double clutching to shift gears. This skill takes practice to learn.

questions.question: During a vehicle inspection, which of the following is NOT required?

options.text: Show that the oil pressure gauge works.
Show that the oil pressure warning light turns off or the gauge shows normal pressure.
Show that the oil temperature gauge rises to normal operating range.
Show that the oil pressure gauge turns on when brakes are used.

questions.correctAnswerText: Show that the oil pressure gauge turns on when brakes are used.
questions.explanation: During an inspection, the oil pressure gauge should work and show normal or increasing pressure. The oil pressure warning light should turn off. If equipped, the oil temperature gauge should gradually rise to normal operating range. The oil pressure gauge does not turn on when brakes are used.

questions.question: What affects how far your vehicle takes to stop?
questions.explanation: Stopping distance depends on how fast you are driving. The faster you go, the longer it takes to stop.

questions.question: In a vehicle with dual parking control valves, what happens when air pressure is lost and spring brakes engage?

options.text: You cannot move the vehicle at all.
A separate air tank can briefly release the spring brakes.
You can continue driving normally with the spring brakes.
The air tanks refill automatically to safe pressure.

questions.correctAnswerText: A separate air tank can briefly release the spring brakes.
questions.explanation: Vehicles with dual parking control valves have a separate air tank that can temporarily release the spring brakes. In an emergency, the driver can use this tank to move the vehicle for a short time.

questions.question: When crossing railroad tracks, you should:
questions.explanation: When crossing railroad tracks, do not stop, change gears, pass another vehicle, or change lanes while any part of your vehicle is on the tracks.

questions.question: Emergency brakes must use what type of force?
questions.explanation: Emergency brakes must use mechanical force. Air pressure can leak away over time, so it cannot be relied on for emergency braking.

questions.question: What happens if you do not drain the air brake system tanks?

options.text: Water can freeze and cause brake failure.
The brakes become soft and squishy.

questions.correctAnswerText: Water can freeze and cause brake failure.
questions.explanation: Air brake system tanks must be drained to remove water and compressor oil. If water builds up and freezes in cold weather, it can cause brake failure.

questions.question: What does an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) do?

options.text: Makes you stop in a shorter distance.
Makes you need a longer distance to stop.
Helps you maintain control while braking.

questions.correctAnswerText: Helps you maintain control while braking.
questions.explanation: ABS helps you stay in control while braking. It does not necessarily make your stopping distance shorter.

questions.question: When entering a highway during the driving test, you should:

options.text: Cut off other drivers if needed.

questions.explanation: When entering a highway during the driving test, you must check for traffic, use your signals, and merge smoothly into the correct lane.

questions.question: Which of the following does NOT cause hydraulic brake failure?
questions.explanation: Hydraulic brake failure usually happens in two ways: loss of hydraulic pressure or overuse on long hills, which causes the brakes to fade.

questions.question: When driving in fog, you will be safest if you:
questions.explanation: Fog reduces your ability to see the road, other vehicles, and hazards. Avoid driving in fog whenever possible.

questions.question: Eating while driving:
questions.explanation: Avoid eating, drinking, or smoking while driving. Any activity that takes your attention away from driving is a distraction.

questions.question: A cardboard box on the road:

options.text: May contain a heavy object that could damage your vehicle.
Should be avoided by leaving the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: May contain a heavy object that could damage your vehicle.
questions.explanation: Any object on the road is potentially dangerous. Something that looks harmless, like a cardboard box, could contain a hard or heavy object that could damage your vehicle.

questions.question: What type of brakes do most heavy-duty vehicles have?
questions.explanation: Most heavy-duty vehicles use dual air brake systems for safety.

questions.question: Where are ABS warning lights located on trucks and buses?

options.text: On the outside by the passenger's door

questions.explanation: Trucks and buses with ABS have yellow warning lights on the instrument panel. Trailers have yellow ABS lights on the left side at the front or rear corner.

questions.question: If a traffic light has been green for a long time:

options.text: It will likely turn yellow soon.
It will likely skip yellow and go straight to red.

questions.correctAnswerText: It will likely turn yellow soon.
questions.explanation: If a traffic light has been green for a long time, it will probably turn yellow before you reach it. Slow down and be ready to stop.

questions.question: Not draining air tanks could result in:

options.text: Water freezing and causing brake failure.
Too much air collecting in the tanks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Water freezing and causing brake failure.
questions.explanation: Air brake tanks must be drained regularly to remove water and compressor oil. If water is not removed, it can freeze in cold weather and cause brake failure.

questions.question: Which of the following shows signs of drowsy driving?

options.text: Eyes losing focus on their own
Having trouble holding your head up

questions.explanation: Signs of drowsiness while driving include eyes losing focus, trouble keeping your head up, and drifting between lanes.

questions.question: If an aggressive driver confronts you, what should you do?
questions.explanation: If an aggressive driver confronts you, move out of their way. Do not make eye contact. Do not react to their gestures. Never speed up to challenge them.

questions.question: During the driving test, how should you change lanes when the examiner asks?

options.text: Use your turn signal and change lanes when it is safe.
Change lanes as fast as possible, even if you cut off another driver.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your turn signal and change lanes when it is safe.
questions.explanation: When the examiner asks you to change lanes, check traffic first. Use your turn signal. Then change lanes only when it is safe.

questions.question: Which crime would NOT disqualify someone from getting a hazardous materials endorsement?
questions.explanation: Kidnapping, smuggling, and immigration violations disqualify you from a hazardous materials endorsement for seven years. More serious crimes like murder result in lifetime disqualification. Speeding does not disqualify you.

questions.question: What is an encroachment?

options.text: A driver does not show up for their basic skills test.
A vehicle touches a boundary line during the basic skills test.
A driver fails one part of the basic skills test.

questions.correctAnswerText: A vehicle touches a boundary line during the basic skills test.
questions.explanation: An encroachment happens when any part of your vehicle touches or crosses a boundary line during the basic skills test. Each encroachment counts as an error.

questions.question: When using a turn signal, what should you NOT do?

options.text: Turn off the signal after completing the turn.
Leave the signal on long after the turn is done.

questions.correctAnswerText: Leave the signal on long after the turn is done.
questions.explanation: Signal well ahead of a turn or lane change. Keep signaling until you finish the turn or lane change. Then turn off the signal so you do not confuse other drivers.

questions.question: If an aggressive driver confronts you, what should you do?

options.text: Make eye contact with the driver.

questions.explanation: If an aggressive driver confronts you, move out of their way. Do not make eye contact. Do not speed up to challenge them. Do not react to their angry gestures.

questions.question: Why were front brake limiting valves designed?

options.text: To stop the front tires from skidding.
To stop the front tires from overheating.
To use brakes equally on all wheels.

questions.correctAnswerText: To stop the front tires from skidding.
questions.explanation: Some older vehicles with air brakes have front brake limiting valves. They were designed to reduce front wheel skidding. However, research shows these valves are not needed. They should be left in the "normal" position.

questions.question: If another vehicle is tailgating you, what should you do?
questions.explanation: If someone is tailgating you, create more space ahead of your vehicle so they can pass safely. Do not speed up, as the driver may continue tailgating at the higher speed, which is more dangerous.

questions.question: What does Gross Vehicle Weight (GVW) mean?

options.text: The total weight of a vehicle plus its load
The total weight of a vehicle's tractor only
The total weight of a loaded trailer only
The weight of a tractor and trailer without the load

questions.correctAnswerText: The total weight of a vehicle plus its load
questions.explanation: Gross Vehicle Weight (GVW) is the total weight of a vehicle plus everything it is carrying.

questions.question: If you need to add coolant to a system without a recovery tank, what should you do first?

options.text: Keep the engine running while adding coolant.
Do not use gloves when touching the radiator cap.
Wait for the engine to cool before adding coolant.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait for the engine to cool before adding coolant.
questions.explanation: Before adding coolant to a system without a recovery tank, turn off the engine and let it cool. Wear gloves or use a thick cloth to protect your hands. Turn the radiator cap slowly to the first stop to release pressure.

questions.question: How can you prevent hydroplaning on wet roads?

options.text: Keep your tires with good tread depth.
Let air out of your tires.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your tires with good tread depth.
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens more on wet roads when tire pressure is too low or tread is worn down. If you start to hydroplane, release the gas and push in the clutch to slow down.

questions.question: What should a commercial motor vehicle have?

options.text: A fire extinguisher only if it carries hazardous materials.
A fire extinguisher only if traveling through remote areas.
A fire extinguisher and other emergency equipment.

questions.correctAnswerText: A fire extinguisher and other emergency equipment.
questions.explanation: All commercial motor vehicles must have emergency equipment. This includes spare fuses, three red reflective triangles or flares, and at least one fire extinguisher that is charged and ready to use.

questions.question: A 10-foot load needs at least how many tie-downs?
questions.explanation: Use at least one tie-down for every 10 feet of cargo. However, all cargo needs at least two tie-downs, no matter the size.

questions.question: What should you do when approaching a railroad crossing?

options.text: You can usually outdrive a train.
Do not rely only on warning signals.
Roll down your window to listen for a train.
Only check the track closest to your vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not rely only on warning signals.
questions.explanation: Never depend only on warning signals to warn you of a train. Never try to race a train. If there are multiple tracks, check all tracks in both directions before crossing.

questions.question: When you push the brake pedal in an air brake system, when do the brakes start working?

options.text: Only when it is warm outside.

questions.explanation: Air takes time to travel through the lines to the brakes. There is a delay of at least half a second between when you press the brake pedal and when the brakes start working.

questions.question: When should you test your service brakes?
questions.explanation: Always check that your service brakes work well before driving. Testing brakes before a trip helps you find problems before you need to brake on the road.

questions.question: Which person should drivers NOT worry about as a distracted person?

options.text: A driver talking to someone in the vehicle.
Children on the side of the road.
Construction workers on the side of the road.
A person sitting on a bench waiting for a bus.

questions.correctAnswerText: A person sitting on a bench waiting for a bus.
questions.explanation: Drivers talking with others may not watch the road carefully and could make unsafe moves. Children can dart into the road without looking. Be careful around road workers to keep them and others safe.

questions.question: What is another name for a front-end header board?
questions.explanation: A front-end header board is also called a "headache rack." It protects the driver if cargo shifts during a crash or sudden stop.

questions.question: When should you check your mirrors?

options.text: When changing lanes only if other vehicles are nearby.
When changing lanes only if it is dark outside.

questions.explanation: Always check your mirrors for traffic before changing lanes. Make mirror checks a regular part of scanning the road.

questions.question: Where should the ABS malfunction lamp be on a dolly?
questions.explanation: A dolly with an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) must have a yellow malfunction lamp on its left side.

questions.question: When loading a trailer, where should you place the weight?

options.text: Only on the left side, if possible.
Only on the right side, if possible.

questions.explanation: Load cargo as low as possible in a trailer. If weight is too high, the trailer may tip over.

questions.question: What do header boards do?

options.text: Protect the driver during a crash.

questions.correctAnswerText: Protect the driver during a crash.
questions.explanation: Header boards protect the driver from cargo that shifts forward during a crash or sudden stop.

questions.question: What happens when you travel down a hill?
questions.explanation: Gravity causes your vehicle to speed up when traveling downhill.

questions.question: When loading a trailer, where should you place the weight?

options.text: As far to the left as possible.

questions.explanation: Cargo with a low center of gravity is less likely to tip over than cargo with a high center of gravity. Always distribute weight as low as possible.

questions.question: What is bracing used for?

options.text: To make items stand taller in a trailer.
To stop items from moving in a trailer.
To make it easier to unload items from a trailer.

questions.correctAnswerText: To stop items from moving in a trailer.
questions.explanation: Bracing prevents cargo from shifting during transport. It connects from the top of cargo down to the floor and sides of the trailer.

questions.question: How do states verify that a driver has only one CDL or CLP license?

options.text: By using a computer system that connects all states.

questions.correctAnswerText: By using a computer system that connects all states.
questions.explanation: All states share CDL and CLP license information in a shared computer database. When you apply for a license, the state checks this database to make sure you don't already have one in another state.

questions.question: When driving at night, which of these should you NOT do?

options.text: Make sure you are well rested.
Make sure your glasses are clean.

questions.explanation: Don't wear sunglasses when driving at night—they reduce visibility. Keep your glasses clean and make sure you are rested before driving at night.

questions.question: What can happen if there is too little weight on a steering axle?
questions.explanation: Cargo weight must be balanced properly. If cargo is placed too far back, the front axle becomes too light. This reduces traction on the front wheels, making steering unsafe.

questions.question: What happens if an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) breaks?

options.text: A yellow warning light appears on the dashboard.

questions.correctAnswerText: A yellow warning light appears on the dashboard.
questions.explanation: A yellow warning light on the dashboard alerts you if the ABS is not working properly.

questions.question: How should you set a front brake limiting valve for normal stopping power?
questions.explanation: Some older vehicles have a front brake limiting valve with "normal" and "slippery" settings. Always leave it in the "normal" position for proper braking.
